page: Microsoft Azure D8alds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Daldsv7 server family. Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, this instance features 8 virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the server is equipped with a 472 GB local disk and is premium storage capable. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng CPU tests and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression workloads, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, including multi-threaded stress-ng and bzip3 decompression, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average throughput, with read-only small block cached memory reaching 905.08 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 49.62 GB/sec. Passmark CPU, encryption, and database operation scores consistently align with mid-tier performance profiles.

Given its low memory-to-CPU ratio, the D8alds_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not demand massive memory footprints. The inclusion of a 472 GB local disk provides high-density local storage without requiring external attachments. This configuration is well-suited for tasks such as single-threaded processing, web serving, lightweight database operations, and general compute workloads where high single-core performance is prioritized over high memory capacity.
